question: A portable CMS designer proposes 'DLY' to mean DELAY. Using Section 1D.08 and Table 1D-3, is this acceptable and why?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No, this is not acceptable. "DLY" appears in Table 1D-3 as an unacceptable abbreviation because it is commonly misinterpreted as "Daily" rather than "Delay," and Section 1D.08 mandates that abbreviations in that table shall not be used on traffic control devices. Since abbreviations on CMS must comply with Section 1D.08, the designer cannot use DLY on a portable changeable message sign. Standards (mandatory): - "The abbreviations shown in Table 1D-3 shall not be used in connection with traffic control devices because of their potential to be misinterpreted by road users." - "Abbreviations displayed on CMS shall comply with the provisions of Section 1D.08." - "When the word messages shown in Table 1D-2 need to be abbreviated on a portable changeable message sign, the abbreviations shown in Table 1D-2 shall be used. Unless indicated by an asterisk, these abbreviations shall only be used on portable changeable message signs." (If "Delay" needs abbreviating, only an abbreviation approved in Table 1D-2 could be used — not DLY.) Guidance (recommended): - If a permissible alternative abbreviation exists in Table 1D-1 or 1D-2 with more than one allowed form, "the same abbreviation should be used throughout a single jurisdiction." Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 1D-3 (Unacceptable Abbreviations), which lists "DLY" with the intended word "Delay" and the common misinterpretation "Daily," confirming that DLY is expressly prohibited. Citations: - Section 1D.08 Standard §4 (p.34) - Section 2L.05 Standard §6 (p.516) - Section 1D.08 Standard §2 (p.34) - Section 1D.08 Guidance §5 (p.34) - Table 1D-3 (p.37)
gold_answer: No. DLY is explicitly prohibited because it can be misinterpreted as DAILY.
